title: Quasi-compact cancellation for algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Give point spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] and use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover. A morphism $a:A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BT$ is quasi-compact for every affine scheme $T\to B$; affine schemes mean spectra of commutative rings [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A morphism is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. If $g\circ f$ is quasi-compact and $g$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is quasi-compact. No quasi-compactness of $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03KS (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence). Affine-test characterization of quasi-compactness: Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), (1) iff (3).

proof.text: First reconcile the conventions. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], a space has quasi-compact point space exactly when it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme. Consequently the affine-test condition in this statement is exactly the affine-test condition of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. That node identifies it with testing all quasi-compact schemes and states stability under arbitrary algebraic-space base change. We use these equivalent conventions below, without assuming that any of the ambient spaces is quasi-compact.

Fix an arbitrary affine scheme $T$ and a map $t:T\to Y$. Form $P=X\times_ZT$, using $gf:X\to Z$ and $gt:T\to Z$, and $Q=X\times_YT$, using $f$ and $t$. These are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. There is a map $e:P\to Y\times_ZY$, $e(x,u)=(f(x),t(u))$, and the natural map $j:Q\to P$ is the pullback of $\Delta_g:Y\to Y\times_ZY$ along $e$. Indeed, on every scheme test a section of that pullback is $(x,u,y)$ with $f(x)=y=t(u)$; deleting $y$ gives precisely a section $(x,u)$ of $Q$, and inserting $f(x)$ is inverse. These maps are natural, hence identify the sheaf fibre products.

source.place: Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), pullback square for the diagonal, specialized to $X	o Y$, $T	o Y$, and $Y	o Z$.

proof.text: Because $gf$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is affine, $P$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis as defined in the statement. Because $g$ is quasi-separated, $\Delta_g$ is quasi-compact. The pullback identity in step 2 and base-change stability in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] show that $j:Q\to P$ is quasi-compact. Step 1 justifies using this node despite its atlas convention. In particular, $Q\times_PU$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact scheme $U\to P$.

Since $P$ is quasi-compact, [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] supplies a quasi-compact scheme $U$ and a representable surjective etale map $U\to P$. Put $R=Q\times_PU$. Step 3 gives quasi-compactness of $R$, so the same equivalence supplies a quasi-compact scheme $V$ with a representable surjective etale map $V\to R$. The projection $R\to Q$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Their composite $V\to Q$ is representable surjective etale: for a scheme $W\to Q$, first $W\times_QR\to W$ is a surjective etale map of schemes, and then $W\times_QV\to W\times_QR$ is one, by the scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The singleton-family case of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] makes the composite scheme test surjective etale. Thus $V\to Q$ is a quasi-compact scheme atlas, and [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] makes $|Q|$ quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact), transitivity argument expanded on atlases; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E4; topologies.tex Tag 0217 (lemma-etale), composition of scheme covers.

proof.text: We have shown that $X\times_YT=Q$ has quasi-compact point space for every affine $T\to Y$. This is exactly the definition of quasi-compactness of $f$ in the statement. If a tested space is empty, the same atlas argument uses the empty scheme as a quasi-compact atlas and all scheme-test assertions remain valid. No step imposed global quasi-compactness on $X$, $Y$, or $Z$.
